title: Iterative tensor network transformations for element-wise evaluation of elementary and filtering functions
authors: Xiao Wang, Tomohiro Hashizume, Pia Siegl, Dieter Jaksch
abstract: Tensor networks are powerful formats for compressing large-scale data. However, their application to general data processing has been limited by the difficulty of performing nonlinear operations. Here, we introduce iterative tensor network transformations (ITNTs), a general algorithmic framework for the element-wise evaluation of elementary and nonlinear filtering functions on data encoded as tensor trains (TTs), a class of tensor networks. Our approach operates entirely in the compressed domain, enabling efficient computation on exponentially large datasets while maintaining a controlled computational cost. We demonstrate its power in two key areas: (I) evaluating highly nonlinear elementary and filtering functions on a 3D reactive flow field, enabling high-fidelity reaction rate computation and region filtering, and (II) finding extrema in complex optimization problems, such as solving Max-SAT instances on spaces up to $2^{70}$ configurations. These results establish ITNT as a foundational tool that provides tensor network methods with the capability for general-purpose data science and large-scale optimization.
summary: The paper introduces Iterative Tensor Network Transformations (ITNT), a novel framework allowing general nonlinear functions to be evaluated directly on data compressed in the Tensor Train format. By leveraging iterative root-finding techniques, ITNT achieves high accuracy for complex physical simulations, such as calculating reaction rates in fluid dynamics and solving NP-hard optimization problems. This establishes tensor networks as a tool for general-purpose, large-scale data science.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing a general algorithmic framework to perform element-wise evaluation of arbitrary, nonlinear filtering functions directly on data encoded in the compressed Tensor Train (TT) format.
main_result: The proposed Iterative Tensor Network Transformations (ITNT) successfully enables high-fidelity computation of nonlinear functions (like reaction rates) and locating global extrema in exponentially large configuration spaces.
method: ITNT utilizes iterative techniques, such as the Newton-Raphson method, combined with efficient TT operations (element-wise product, partial integration) to operate entirely in the compressed domain.
model_or_system: The methods are demonstrated on several models: 3D reactive flow fields (methane/air jet flame) for continuous field evaluation, and classical Ising models/Max-SAT instances for combinatorial optimization.
key_observables: Reaction rates (Arrhenius factor), global energy extrema ($E_{opt}$), and the relative $\ell_2$ error ($	ilde{\epsilon}$).
important_parameters: Bond dimension ($\chi$), number of iterations ($N_{	ext{iter}}$), and the required preprocessing steps (e.g., self-multiplication power $P$).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that the required functions can be mapped to iterative root-finding problems solvable via the Newton-Raphson method or related fixed-point iterations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the methodology for nonlinear evaluation (Fig. 1a, 1b) and the application to optimization, showing convergence comparisons between ITNT and interpolation methods (TCI).
paper_structure: The paper introduces ITNT, details its application to continuous nonlinear PDEs (reactive flow), and then extends it to discrete, high-dimensional optimization problems like Max-SAT and Ising model energy matching.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general-purpose computational tool that extends tensor network methods beyond linear operations, making them applicable to complex, nonlinear physics problems previously requiring computationally expensive full-space sampling.
